args: Analyze the contiguous-memory branch of `frame_get_lazychunk()` in `c-blosc2/blosc/frame.c` lines 2016-2032. What exact overflow-safe validation should be used after `blosc2_cbuffer_sizes()` to ensure the entire claimed chunk lies within the actual `frame->cframe` allocation represented by `frame->len`? Also identify relevant signedness/range properties of `header_len`, `offset`, and parsed `lazychunk_cbytes`.

The supplied ASan report shows an out-of-bounds dictionary-size read during decompression. In the contiguous branch, the current code computes `chunk_header_offset = header_len + offset`, verifies only `chunk_header_offset + BLOSC_MIN_HEADER_LENGTH`, parses the chunk, and then incorrectly checks `if (rc && chunk_cbytes_offset + lazychunk_cbytes > frame_len)`. Successful parsing returns zero, so oversized `cbytes` is accepted. The requested root fix must handle parser errors separately and always validate the complete extent from `chunk_header_offset` against the real backing length (`frame->len`) with overflow-safe arithmetic. I am considering subtraction-based checks rather than addition and want to preserve valid frames.
